results.summary_before: This design is a guitar tuner that counts rising edges of an input pulse over a fixed sampling period and compares the count to frequencies of interest for standard guitar tuning, covering notes from about 80 to 400 Hz. It supports multiple clock configurations via three input bits and can drive either a dual or single 7-segment display, with the dot indicating an exact match in single mode. The raw pulse count is output on the bidirectional pins, and testing requires feeding a variable frequency signal and observing the closest note on the display. A silicon test report confirms it works, showing the closest note for a variable frequency input.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 256-byte ROM that stores information about the Tiny Tapeout chip. The ROM is 8 bits wide and is accessed by setting the address pins and reading the data pins. The first 16 bytes are 7-segment encoded and contain the shuttle name and commit hash, which can be displayed on the on-board 7-segment display. No external hardware is required beyond the standard board.
